metrics.caveat: The platform publishes subscriber counts rounded above 1,000, so a channel sitting on a 1,000 threshold cannot be resolved either way from the public figure.

metrics.display_name: Valid public uploads in the last 90 days
metrics.caveat: Counted from the public upload list. The rule counts VALID public uploads and validity is a platform determination, so a channel sitting on the minimum may still be judged short.

metrics.display_name: Qualified watch hours in the last 12 months
metrics.caveat: Watch time is not published on any public account surface. It cannot be derived from public view counts: doing so would require assuming an average viewed duration, which is exactly the estimate this contract keeps out of eligibility decisions.
metrics.what_would_unblock: An authorized owner analytics path for the creator's own channel. No public path can ever settle this gate.

metrics.display_name: Qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days
metrics.caveat: Public Shorts view counts are not the platform's qualified Shorts views; the platform excludes some views from the qualified figure. A public total is therefore an upper bound: it can show a channel is short of the threshold, never that it has cleared it.
metrics.what_would_unblock: An authorized owner analytics path reporting the qualified figure directly.

metrics.caveat: Access is offered by the platform rather than applied for, and the bar is not published. No data path settles this.

metrics.caveat: Summed over a bounded window of recent posts. Set coverage_complete honestly: when the window does not reach back the full period, the total undercounts and settles nothing.
metrics.what_would_unblock: A retrieval depth that reliably covers 30 days of posting for a high-frequency account.

metrics.what_would_unblock: A retrieval depth that reliably covers 30 days of posting for a high-frequency account.

metrics.caveat: No public source carries a per-channel RPM, and the YouTube Analytics API does not return RPM as a metric: checked 2026-09-14 against its metric list, which names estimatedRevenue but no RPM. The earlier wording here went further and said revenue itself is unavailable to a channel report; that is not what the metric list shows, and it is why this entry previously read as a dead end.

provenance.note: TikTok publishes no per-account RPM. This band is what creators themselves report, and the calculator says so at source: 「是 creator-reported 口径——TikTok 不公布官方 RPM，这个带宽在创作者社区的公开分享里反复出现」。It is the only rate in this library that is neither published by the platform nor chosen by us, and it may only ever be shown as a range described that way. Unlike the YouTube RPM figures in the same product - which disagree with each other by roughly 2x and carry no provenance at all - there is exactly one of these and it is labelled at source.

niche_rates.note: YouTube does not publish a rate per content niche. Its own revenue analytics page defines RPM and CPM and lists what RPM is made of, with no figure for any niche. Tables that rank niches by RPM come from third parties, and this library carries only what a platform states or, labelled as such, what creators report for a programme.
